platform_split_2026_08_03.source: RevenueCat customer records (first_seen_at, last_seen_platform), cross-checked against PostHog $os.
platform_split_2026_08_03.ios_installs: 129 was WRONG (RevenueCat). Apple says 51 first-time downloads lifetime to 2026-08-20 (DEC-321). RevenueCat inflated iOS by 2.5x, Android by ~6x. See appstore_funnel_2026_08_27.
platform_split_2026_08_03.ios_rate_pct: 2.33 was WRONG and must not be quoted (corrected by DEC-340, 2026-09-17). It divided real App Store sales by RevenueCat's iOS customer count, which DEC-334 measured to be ~2x Apple's real install count. On Apple's own App Downloads report the rate is 3 of 51 first-time downloads = 5.9% (Wilson 2.0-15.9%) over the clean window 2026-04-25..08-20, and 4.0-5.9% all time because the 4th sale falls inside the 16-day handover hole.
platform_split_2026_08_03.posthog_agrees: PostHog $os: Android 217 people, iOS 80. Same direction, ~70% Android, from an independent system.
platform_split_2026_08_03.android_is_not_broken: Play Store billing is PROVEN WORKING: two play_store SANDBOX purchases validated through RevenueCat on 2026-05-10. Android's zero is genuine demand, not a misconfigured integration. Do NOT open a 'fix Android billing' ticket.
platform_split_2026_08_03.android_reaches_the_paywall_more: 46 Android people reached the paywall vs 28 iOS. All 9 Android purchase-shaped paywall_result events are build 22 (internal testing, May) plus one sandbox on 2026-07-01.
platform_split_2026_08_03.implication: Every ASO decision we have made targets the App Store, which is ~31% of installs and 100% of revenue. That focus is correct, for a reason we did not know until now. Android acquisition is worth ~zero until one Android buyer exists.
platform_split_2026_08_03.open_discrepancy: Play Console's public listing says '10+ downloads' but RevenueCat counts 287 Android installs and PostHog 217 people, spread across all 8 released versions. Benedict can see the real Play Console number; worth one look.

purchase_lag_2026_08_03.finding: ALL THREE buyers purchased on the SAME DAY they installed. Lag 0, 0, 0.
purchase_lag_2026_08_03.why_it_matters: Nobody has ever installed, used Treesmith, and later decided to pay. The purchase decision is made from the store listing and the first-run impression, before the product is experienced.
purchase_lag_2026_08_03.reframes: Activation and retention sit DOWNSTREAM of the money, not upstream. DEC-252's 'activation is the constraint' and DEC-254's 'retention is the real open question' are both true about the product and neither is currently a revenue lever. Store listing, price and first-run are.
purchase_lag_2026_08_03.cohort_evidence: Because lag is 0, cohort maturity does not confound: the May cohort's 48 iOS installs had their chance on day 1 and took it 0 times. iOS by month: Mar 5/0, Apr 33/0, May 48/0, Jun 19/1, Jul 22/2.
purchase_lag_2026_08_03.caveat: n=3. Stated as the strongest signal we have about WHEN the decision is made, not as an established rate.

body.install_count_divergence: RevenueCat 416 customers vs PostHog 297 people (+40%). Neither is authoritative: RevenueCat opens a customer per SDK init, PostHog merges aliased ids onto a person. The digest now prints the gap rather than picking one and quietly dividing by it. Retention cross-check: RevenueCat says 11% of iOS and 5% of Android are ever seen on a later day; 272 of 287 Android and 111 of 129 iOS are never seen again 60s after first launch.
body.latest_sweep: Re-swept 2026-09-17: 4 production purchases, US$70.04 proceeds, US$102.57 gross, MRR US$0. The 4th (2026-08-23, US, iPad, build 1.0.10) is the first sale after either rename and was missed until now. Still 0 Android and 0 Cloud Backup sales.
